column1: Collecting must be one of the most varied of human activities, and it’s one that many of us psychologists find fascinating.
column2: 收藏大概是人类活动中形式最多样的活动之一，也让我们许多心理学家深感着迷。

column1: Many forms of collecting have been dignified with a technical name: an archtophilist collects teddy bears, a philatelist collects postage stamps, and a deltiologist collects postcards.
column2: 不少收藏活动还有煞有介事的专名：archtophilist收藏泰迪熊，philatelist集邮，deltiologist则收藏明信片。

column1: Amassing hundreds or even thousands of postcards, chocolate wrappers or whatever, takes time, energy and money that could surely be put to much more productive use.
column2: 攒下成百上千张明信片、巧克力包装纸之类的东西，要花费时间、精力和金钱，而这些投入显然可以用在更富有成效的事情上。
column5: or whatever|或诸如此类的东西

column1: And yet there are millions of collectors around the world.
column2: 然而，世界各地有数以百万计的收藏者。

column1: Why do they do it?
column2: 他们为什么要收藏呢？

column1: There are the people who collect because they want to make money - this could be called an instrumental reason for collecting; that is, collecting as a means to an end.
column2: 有些人收藏是为了赚钱。我们可以把这称为收藏的工具性动机，也就是说，收藏是达到另一目的的手段。
column6: a means to an end|达到目的的手段

column1: They’ll look for, say, antiques that they can buy cheaply and expect to be able to sell at a profit.
column2: 比如，他们会寻找能低价买入、又有望转卖获利的古董。
column6: sell at a profit|转卖获利

column1: But there may well be a psychological element, too — buying cheap and selling dear can give the collector a sense of triumph.
column2: 但其中很可能还有心理因素：低买高卖能让收藏者感受到胜利的喜悦。

column1: And as selling online is so easy, more and more people are joining in.
column2: 而且，由于网上出售物品十分方便，加入的人越来越多。

column1: Many collectors collect to develop their social life, attending meetings of a group of collectors and exchanging information on items.
column2: 许多收藏者借收藏来拓展社交生活：他们参加同好的聚会，交流藏品信息。
column3: develop their social life|拓展社交生活

column1: This is a variant on joining a bridge club or a gym, and similarly brings them into contact with like-minded people.
column2: 这和加入桥牌俱乐部或健身房有异曲同工之处，同样让他们有机会结识志同道合的人。

column1: Another motive for collecting is the desire to find something special, or a particular example of the collected item, such as a rare early recording by a particular singer.
column2: 另一种收藏动机是想找到特别的东西，或是某一类藏品中的特定一件，例如某位歌手一份罕见的早期录音。
column5: a particular example|一个特定实例
column7: rare early recording|罕见的早期录音

column1: Some may spend their whole lives in a hunt for this.
column2: 有些人可能终其一生都在寻找这件东西。
column3: spend their whole lives|花上一辈子
column4: in a hunt for|在寻找……的过程中

column1: Psychologically, this can give a purpose to a life that otherwise feels aimless.
column2: 从心理上说，这能给原本似乎漫无目标的人生赋予一个目标。

column1: There is a danger, though, that if the individual is ever lucky enough to find what they’re looking for, rather than celebrating their success, they may feel empty, now that the goal that drove them on has gone.
column2: 不过，其中也有风险。如果这个人真有幸找到了自己寻觅的东西，他可能非但不庆祝成功，反而感到空虚，因为一直推动他前进的目标已经消失了。
column9: drove them on|激励他们不断前进

column1: If you think about collecting postage stamps, another potential reason for it — or, perhaps, a result of collecting — is its educational value.
column2: 以集邮为例，另一个可能的收藏动机，或者说收藏带来的一种结果，就是它的教育价值。
column5: a result of collecting|收藏的结果

column1: Stamp collecting opens a window to other countries, and to the plants, animals, or famous people shown on their stamps.
column2: 集邮为人打开了一扇窗，让人了解其他国家，也了解那些国家邮票上印的植物、动物或知名人物。
column4: opens a window to|打开了解……的一扇窗

column1: Similarly, in the 19th century, many collectors amassed fossils, animals and plants from around the globe, and their collections provided a vast amount of information about the natural world.
column2: 同样，19世纪许多收藏者从世界各地搜集化石、动物和植物，他们的收藏为认识自然界提供了大量信息。

column1: Without those collections, our understanding would be greatly inferior to what it is.
column2: 没有那些收藏，我们对自然界的认识会比现在浅薄得多。

column1: In the past — and nowadays, too, though to a lesser extent — a popular form of collecting, particularly among boys and men, was trainspotting.
column2: 过去有一种很受欢迎的收藏活动，尤其受男孩和成年男子青睐，就是观察火车、记录机车。如今也有人这么做，只是没那么盛行了。
column4: to a lesser extent|程度较轻
column6: trainspotting|n. 观察火车并记录机车的爱好

column1: This might involve trying to see every locomotive of a particular type, using published data that identifies each one, and ticking off each engine as it is seen.
column2: 爱好者有时会设法见到某一型号的每一台机车。他们用公开资料辨认不同的机车，每见到一台就在清单上勾掉一项。
column7: ticking off|从清单上逐一勾去

column1: Trainspotters exchange information, these days often by mobile phone, so they can work out where to go to, to see a particular engine.
column2: 火车观察爱好者互通信息，现在常用手机联系，这样就能弄清要看某一台机车该去哪里。
column7: a particular engine|某一台特定机车

column1: As a by-product, many practitioners of the hobby become very knowledgeable about railway operations, or the technical specifications of different engine types.
column2: 作为这项爱好的附带收获，许多爱好者会对铁路运营或不同型号机车的技术规格相当了解。
column4: practitioners|n. 从事这项活动的人

column1: Similarly, people who collect dolls may go beyond simply enlarging their collection, and develop an interest in the way that dolls are made, or the materials that are used.
column2: 同样，收藏玩偶的人可能不满足于简单增加藏品，还会对玩偶的制作方法或所用材料产生兴趣。
column5: develop an interest in|对……产生兴趣

column1: These have changed over the centuries from the wood that was standard in 16th century Europe, through the wax and porcelain of later centuries, to the plastics of today’s dolls.
column2: 几个世纪来，这些材料一直在变：16世纪欧洲通常用木料，后来的几个世纪用蜡和瓷，如今的玩偶则用塑料。
column3: over the centuries|几个世纪以来

column1: Or collectors might be inspired to study how dolls reflect notions of what children like, or ought to like.
column2: 收藏者也可能由此产生研究兴趣，想知道玩偶如何反映人们关于儿童喜欢什么、又应该喜欢什么的看法。

column1: Not all collectors are interested in learning from their hobby, though, so what we might call a psychological reason for collecting is the need for a sense of control, perhaps as a way of dealing with insecurity.
column2: 然而，并非所有收藏者都想从这项爱好中学到东西。我们所说的一种心理动机，是人有获得掌控感的需要，也许是想以此应对内心的不安。

column1: Stamp collectors, for instance, arrange their stamps in albums, usually very neatly, organising their collection according to certain commonplace principles - perhaps by country in alphabetical order, or grouping stamps by what they depict — people, birds, maps, and so on.
column2: 比如，集邮者通常将邮票整整齐齐地排入集邮册，按某些常见原则整理藏品：可能按国名字母顺序排列，也可能根据邮票上画的是人物、鸟、地图还是其他东西来分组。

column1: One reason, conscious or not, for what someone chooses to collect is to show the collector’s individualism.
column2: 一个人选择收藏某样东西，背后的原因之一是彰显其个性，无论他本人是否意识到这一点。

column1: Someone who decides to collect something as unexpected as dog collars, for instance, may be conveying their belief that they must be interesting themselves.
column2: 比如，选择收藏狗项圈这样出人意料的东西，可能是在传达一种想法：自己想必也是个有趣的人。

column1: And believe it or not, there is at least one dog collar museum in existence, and it grew out of a personal collection.
column2: 信不信由你，确实至少有一家狗项圈博物馆，它就是从私人收藏发展而来的。
column3: believe it or not|信不信由你

column1: Of course, all hobbies give pleasure, but the common factor in collecting is usually passion: pleasure is putting it far too mildly.
column2: 当然，所有爱好都会带来乐趣，但收藏往往还有一个共同点，那就是热爱。只用“乐趣”来形容，实在说得太轻了。
column6: putting it far too mildly|说得实在太轻了

column1: More than most other hobbies, collecting can be totally engrossing, and can give a strong sense of personal fulfilment.
column2: 比起其他大多数爱好，收藏更能让人全神贯注，并带来强烈的个人成就感。
column5: a strong sense of|强烈的……感

column1: To non-collectors it may appear an eccentric, if harmless, way of spending time, but potentially, collecting has a lot going for it.
column2: 在不收藏的人看来，这种消遣方式也许无害却有些古怪；不过，收藏有不少潜在的好处。
column7: has a lot going for it|有许多可取之处
